passages.title: The Quiet Partnership
passages.text:
Lichens are often mistaken for a single organism, yet each one is a partnership: a fungus provides structure and shelter, while an alga or cyanobacterium living among its threads manufactures food through photosynthesis. For over a century, biologists described the arrangement as mutual benefit, but some researchers now argue that the fungus is, in effect, a gentle farmer that keeps its partner in captivity, since the alga can often survive alone whereas the fungus rarely can. Whatever the truth, the union is remarkably successful. Lichens colonise bare rock, tree bark and even Antarctic stones where almost nothing else survives, and over centuries their acids slowly break rock into the first thin soil on which mosses and flowering plants later settle.

Because lichens have no roots or protective skin, they absorb water and dissolved substances directly from the air. This makes them poor survivors in polluted cities but excellent witnesses. Several species disappear when sulphur dioxide rises, and their return to city trees is therefore read by ecologists as evidence that the air is improving. It would be unwise, however, to treat any single species as a perfect gauge; moisture, the age of the tree and the acidity of its bark also decide which lichens grow, and a bare trunk does not always indicate pollution.

passages.title: The Potter's Wheel
passages.text:
He bends above the turning clay
As though in prayer, not toil,
And lets the slow wheel say for him
What hands alone would spoil.

A press too hard, the vessel bursts;
Too light, it will not stand.
So patience is the secret skill
That guides the shaping hand.

The clay remembers every touch
And keeps what it is shown;
A tremor in the potter's thumb
Will harden into stone.

The kiln will test what he has made
With fire he cannot ease;
Some pots will ring and some will crack,
And neither one he sees

Until the heat has gone. He waits,
Unhurried, by the door;
For all his art is learning how
To wish, and then no more.

passages.title: The Idle Room
passages.text:
SCENE: The verandah of a village school. MEERA, the headmistress, is arranging books. RAMLAL, the Sarpanch, enters with a file.

RAMLAL: Headmistress, the panchayat has a proposal. Your library room is lying idle. We could rent it to the grain cooperative.
MEERA: Idle? Come on a Saturday, Sarpanchji. Twenty children sit on that floor from morning until the caretaker locks up.
RAMLAL: (glancing at the file) The register shows only nine books issued last month.
MEERA: The register shows what the children carried home. It does not show what they read standing between the shelves, because their fathers need the lamp at night.
RAMLAL: Sentiment will not pay for the new roof.
MEERA: Neither will a bag of rice, if the roof shelters children who cannot read the label on it.
RAMLAL: (after a pause, softening) You argue as though I were an enemy of the school.
MEERA: Not an enemy. Merely a man who has measured the room, and not what it holds.
RAMLAL: Hm. Perhaps I should visit on Saturday.

questions.question: It is high time the government ___ stringent measures against adulteration.
questions.explanation: "It is (high) time + subject" is followed by the past subjunctive form, so "took" is correct although the sense is present.

questions.question: Not until the audit was completed ___ the extent of the fraud.
questions.explanation: After "Not until + clause" the main clause takes inversion with an auxiliary: "did the board discover". The other forms lack inversion or use the wrong tense.

questions.question: The committee insisted that the secretary ___ the minutes before Friday.
questions.explanation: After verbs like insist/demand/recommend, the mandative subjunctive uses the bare infinitive: "submit". The other forms are indicative.

questions.question: She said, "I have been waiting here since morning." The correct indirect form is:
options: She said that she has been waiting here since morning.
She said that she was waiting there since morning.
She said that she had been waiting there since morning.
She said that she had waited here since morning.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous, and "here" becomes "there". Option 2 keeps the tense and place unchanged; options 3 and 4 change the aspect.

questions.question: The teacher reminded the class that water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps the present tense even after a past reporting verb, so "boils" is correct.

questions.question: She is one of those teachers who ___ never tired of correcting notebooks.
questions.explanation: In "one of those ... who", the relative pronoun refers to the plural "teachers", so the verb is plural: "are". Singular forms or past tense are wrong here.

questions.question: The lights were off and his car was gone, so he ___ at home when we called.
questions.explanation: "Can't have been" expresses a strong negative deduction about the past. "Needn't have been" means unnecessary action; the others do not carry past reference.

questions.question: There is ___ hope of his recovery; the doctors have almost given up.
questions.explanation: "Little" (without a) gives a negative sense: almost none. "A little" is positive; few/a few go with countable nouns, and hope is uncountable here.

questions.question: Not only the students but also the teacher ___ responsible for the delay.
questions.explanation: With "not only... but also" the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "the teacher", which is singular and present here: "is".

questions.question: Which of the following is an it-cleft sentence?
options: What Gandhi led was the Salt March.
The Salt March was led by Gandhi.
It was Gandhi who led the Salt March.
Led by Gandhi, the march reached Dandi.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft has the structure "It + be + focus + clause". Option 2 is a wh- (pseudo-)cleft, option 3 a plain passive and option 4 a participial phrase.

questions.question: I haven't seen the film, but my sister ___.
questions.explanation: The auxiliary "has" substitutes for "has seen it" (elliptical). "Have" does not agree with the singular subject; did/does do not match the present perfect.

questions.question: Convert into a complex sentence: "Being poor, he could not buy the book."
options: He was poor and he could not buy the book.
Though he was poor, he could not buy the book.
If he were poor, he could not buy the book.
As he was poor, he could not buy the book.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase of reason becomes a subordinate clause of reason ("As he was poor"). Option 2 is compound; options 3 and 4 change the meaning (concession/condition).

questions.question: By the time the rescue team arrived, the villagers ___ for help for two days.
questions.explanation: "By the time" + past simple needs the past perfect continuous for the earlier, ongoing action. The other tenses do not fit a past reference point.

questions.question: The minister's careless remark ___ a storm of protest.
questions.explanation: "Set off" = to cause to start. "Set in" = begin (of bad weather/decay), "set about" = begin doing, "set aside" = reserve/ignore.

questions.question: In "She is said to have left the country", the phrase "to have left" is a:
questions.explanation: "To have + past participle" is the perfect infinitive. A participle or gerund would not take "to", and the phrase is non-finite, not finite.

questions.question: "Pusillanimous" means
questions.explanation: Pusillanimous (Latin pusillus + animus) means timid and cowardly.

questions.question: Which word contains a prefix meaning "around"?
questions.explanation: Circum- = around (circumnavigate = sail around). Contra- = against, sub- = under, inter- = between.

questions.question: In which sentence does "strike" mean "to discover suddenly"?
options: The workers decided to strike from Monday.
She struck a pose for the camera.
The drillers struck oil at 300 metres.
questions.explanation: "Struck oil" = found it. The other uses mean sounded, stop work and adopt, respectively.

questions.question: The red scarf was a perfect ___ to her black dress.
questions.explanation: Complement = something that completes or goes well with. Compliment = praise; supplement = an addition; implement = tool.

questions.question: A ___ of bees was seen hanging from the branch.
questions.explanation: Collocation restricts the collective noun: a swarm of bees. Pack (wolves), herd (cattle), shoal (fish).

questions.question: In "She elbowed her way through the crowd", the word "elbowed" is formed by conversion from a
questions.explanation: Conversion changes the word class without any affix: the noun "elbow" is used as a verb.

questions.question: Which lexical bundle signals concession?
questions.explanation: "Having said that" introduces a contrasting/concessive point. The others express result, condition and cause.

questions.question: "To steal a march on someone" means to
options: gain an advantage over them by acting first
questions.explanation: The idiom comes from the military sense of marching ahead of an opponent unnoticed.

questions.question: "Quixotic" describes a person or plan that is
questions.explanation: From Cervantes' Don Quixote; quixotic means romantically idealistic with little regard for practicality.

questions.question: A harsh, jarring combination of sounds in a line of verse is called
questions.explanation: Cacophony is deliberately harsh-sounding language; euphony is its pleasant opposite.

questions.question: A sudden fall from the sublime to the ridiculous in speech or writing is called
questions.explanation: Bathos is an anticlimax; pathos evokes pity, and climax is a rising order of intensity.

questions.question: "Ephemeral" means
options: lasting for a very short time
questions.explanation: From Greek ephemeros ("for a day"): short-lived.

questions.question: A play on words that exploits similar sounds or double meanings is called
questions.explanation: Paronomasia is the technical name for a pun.

questions.question: Which line is an example of epistrophe?
options: They demanded freedom; they fought for freedom; they died for freedom.
Fair is foul, and foul is fair.
I came, I saw, I conquered.
questions.explanation: Epistrophe repeats the same word at the END of successive clauses ("freedom"). Option 2 is epizeuxis, option 3 chiasmus (antimetabole) and option 4 asyndeton.

questions.question: The suffix "-escent" in "adolescent" means
questions.explanation: -escent (from Latin -escere) means growing or becoming, so adolescent = growing up. -ful, -less and -able give the other meanings.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
options: Lichens grow best in the most polluted cities.
Lichens take in water directly from the air.
Lichens living on rock help form the first soil.
The acidity of bark affects which lichens grow on a tree.
questions.explanation: The passage says several lichens disappear when sulphur dioxide rises, so growing best in polluted cities contradicts it. The other statements are stated directly.

questions.question: In the passage, lichens are called "excellent witnesses" because they
questions.explanation: "Witnesses" is used figuratively: lichens give evidence of pollution levels. They are, in fact, "poor survivors" in polluted cities, so option 3 is wrong.

questions.question: The author's attitude to using lichens as pollution indicators is best described as
questions.explanation: The author values them but warns "it would be unwise to treat any single species as a perfect gauge" - appreciation with caution.

questions.question: The phrase "a gentle farmer that keeps its partner in captivity" is a
questions.explanation: The fungus is directly described as a farmer without "like/as": a metaphor.

questions.question: The passage is chiefly concerned with showing that lichens
options: are plants that grow only in unpolluted places.
always exploit the algae that live inside them.
are ecologically important fungus-alga partnerships whose value as pollution indicators needs careful interpretation.
are governed in their distribution by sulphur dioxide alone.
questions.explanation: The passage covers the partnership, soil-building and indicator use with caveats. Options 2, 3 and 4 are over-generalisations that the passage denies.

questions.question: "As though in prayer, not toil" contains a
questions.explanation: The comparison is introduced by "as though": simile.

questions.question: The lines "A tremor in the potter's thumb / Will harden into stone" suggest that
options: the potter's thumb is made of stone
faults in handling become permanent once the pot is fired
questions.explanation: The clay "remembers every touch"; a slip is fixed permanently in the fired pot. The rest take the image literally.

questions.question: The last two lines, "learning how / To wish, and then no more", mean that the potter must
options: hope for success but accept what he cannot control
questions.explanation: After doing his best he can only wish; the firing outcome is beyond his control.

questions.question: The second stanza of the poem chiefly conveys that
options: strength is the potter's chief virtue
pots must be made as thin as possible
good pottery needs patient, balanced pressure
questions.explanation: "Too hard, it bursts; too light, it will not stand" shows balance, and the stanza names patience as the secret skill.

questions.question: "And neither one he sees / Until the heat has gone" implies that the potter
options: learns the result of firing only after the kiln cools
questions.explanation: The potter cannot see whether pots ring or crack until the heat is gone; he waits by the door, so he does not leave.

questions.question: Meera's remark about the register implies that it
options: is deliberately falsified by the staff
understates the real use of the library
shows that books are not needed
questions.explanation: Children read in the library without taking books home, so issue figures undercount use.

questions.question: Meera's reply, "Neither will a bag of rice, if the roof shelters children who cannot read the label on it", is
questions.explanation: She turns his practical argument against him with sharp irony while remaining polite.

questions.question: At the beginning of the scene, Ramlal's attitude to the library is mainly
questions.explanation: He judges the room by its economic use (rent, register), a practical or utilitarian approach, though he is not hostile.

questions.question: Meera's last line, "a man who has measured the room, and not what it holds", chiefly uses
questions.explanation: It contrasts the room's size with its contents: antithesis. There is no sound imitation, wordplay or address to an absent person.

questions.question: The scene ends with Ramlal
options: showing the first sign of a changed attitude
questions.explanation: He softens and says he might visit on Saturday, suggesting a partial change of heart, not a decision to rent.

questions.question: According to Swain's Output Hypothesis, producing the target language helps acquisition mainly because it
questions.questionHi: स्वेन की Output Hypothesis के अनुसार लक्ष्य भाषा बोलना या लिखना अधिगम में मुख्यतः इसलिए सहायक है क्योंकि यह
options: replaces the need for any input
makes learners notice gaps in their own knowledge
optionsHi: इनपुट की ज़रूरत को खत्म कर देता है
सीखने वाले को अपने ज्ञान की कमियों का ध्यान कराता है
affective filter को हटा देता है
questions.explanation: Swain argued that pushed output makes learners notice what they cannot yet say and test hypotheses. It complements, not replaces, input; the affective filter is Krashen's idea.
questions.explanationHi: स्वेन के अनुसार "pushed output" से सीखने वाला जान पाता है कि वह क्या नहीं कह पा रहा और अपनी परिकल्पनाओं को परखता है। यह input का विकल्प नहीं, पूरक है; affective filter क्रैशेन की अवधारणा है।

questions.question: The strong form of Lado's Contrastive Analysis Hypothesis predicts that learning difficulty arises mainly where
questions.questionHi: लाडो की Contrastive Analysis Hypothesis का प्रबल रूप भविष्यवाणी करता है कि सीखने की कठिनाई मुख्यतः वहाँ होती है जहाँ
options: the structures of the mother tongue and the target language differ
the teacher uses the mother tongue
the target language has a long literature
optionsHi: मातृभाषा और लक्ष्य भाषा की संरचनाएँ भिन्न होती हैं
शिक्षक मातृभाषा का प्रयोग करता है
लक्ष्य भाषा का साहित्य बहुत लंबा होता है
questions.explanation: Lado held that differences between L1 and L2 cause difficulty and errors, while similarities facilitate transfer. Later research showed many errors are not predicted this way.
questions.explanationHi: लाडो के अनुसार L1 और L2 के अंतर कठिनाई और त्रुटियाँ पैदा करते हैं, जबकि समानताएँ अंतरण में सहायक होती हैं। बाद के शोध में अनेक त्रुटियाँ इस प्रकार अनुमानित नहीं पाई गईं।

questions.question: According to Cummins' Linguistic Interdependence Hypothesis, skills developed in the first language
questions.questionHi: कमिंस की Linguistic Interdependence Hypothesis के अनुसार पहली भाषा में विकसित कौशल
options: interfere with L2 and must be suppressed
are lost once L2 instruction starts
can transfer to the second language through a common underlying proficiency
optionsHi: L2 में बाधा डालते हैं और उन्हें दबाना चाहिए
L2 शिक्षण शुरू होते ही खो जाते हैं
एक साझा अंतर्निहित दक्षता (common underlying proficiency) के माध्यम से दूसरी भाषा में स्थानांतरित हो सकते हैं
questions.explanation: Cummins argued that L1 and L2 share a common underlying proficiency, so literacy and concepts built in L1 support L2.
questions.explanationHi: कमिंस के अनुसार L1 और L2 की दक्षता का आधार साझा है, इसलिए L1 में बनी साक्षरता और अवधारणाएँ L2 की मदद करती हैं।

questions.question: According to Cummins, Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (CALP) in a second language generally takes
questions.questionHi: कमिन्स के अनुसार द्वितीय भाषा में Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (CALP) विकसित होने में सामान्यतः लगते हैं
options: about five to seven years to develop
no time, since it is innate
optionsHi: कोई समय नहीं, क्योंकि यह जन्मजात है
questions.explanation: Cummins found BICS (conversational fluency) appears in about 1–2 years, but CALP (academic language) typically needs 5–7 years.
questions.explanationHi: कमिन्स के अनुसार BICS (बोलचाल की प्रवाहिता) 1-2 वर्ष में आ जाती है, पर CALP (शैक्षणिक भाषा) में सामान्यतः 5-7 वर्ष लगते हैं।

questions.question: A child who keeps asking "Why does it rain?" is using, in Halliday's terms, the
questions.questionHi: हैलिडे के अनुसार जो बच्चा बार-बार पूछता है "बारिश क्यों होती है?", वह भाषा का कौन-सा प्रकार्य प्रयोग कर रहा है?
questions.explanation: The heuristic function is language used to learn and explore the environment (asking questions). Regulatory controls behaviour, personal expresses identity, instrumental satisfies needs.
questions.explanationHi: Heuristic function में भाषा का उपयोग सीखने-खोजने (प्रश्न पूछने) के लिए होता है। Regulatory व्यवहार नियंत्रित करता है, personal पहचान व्यक्त करता है, instrumental ज़रूरतें पूरी करता है।

questions.question: Hymes criticised Chomsky's notion of competence mainly because it ignored
questions.questionHi: हाइम्स ने चॉम्स्की की competence की अवधारणा की मुख्य आलोचना इसलिए की क्योंकि वह उपेक्षा करती थी
options: knowing what is appropriate in a given social context
optionsHi: किसी सामाजिक संदर्भ में क्या उचित है, इसके ज्ञान की
questions.explanation: Hymes added sociolinguistic appropriateness: knowing when, where and to whom to say what. He did not reject syntax or innateness as such.
questions.explanationHi: हाइम्स ने सामाजिक-भाषिक उपयुक्तता जोड़ी: कब, कहाँ और किससे क्या कहना है। उन्होंने वाक्य-विन्यास या जन्मजात क्षमता को नकारा नहीं।

questions.question: A learner forgets the word "umbrella" and says "the thing you hold over your head when it rains". In Canale and Swain's model, this shows
questions.questionHi: कैनेल और स्वेन के मॉडल में, जब सीखने वाला "umbrella" शब्द भूलकर कहता है "वह चीज़ जिसे बारिश में सिर के ऊपर पकड़ते हैं", तो यह दर्शाता है
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing to overcome a gap in vocabulary is a communication strategy: strategic competence.
questions.explanationHi: शब्द-भंडार की कमी को वैकल्पिक कथन से पूरा करना संप्रेषण-रणनीति है: strategic competence।

questions.question: Unlike contrastive analysis, which predicts difficulty from L1-L2 differences, error analysis studies
questions.questionHi: Contrastive analysis जहाँ L1-L2 के अंतर से कठिनाई का अनुमान लगाता है, वहीं error analysis अध्ययन करता है
options: the actual errors found in learners' output
optionsHi: केवल सीखने वाले की मातृभाषा का
सीखने वाले के वास्तविक प्रयोग में मिलीं त्रुटियों का
questions.explanation: Error analysis (Corder) examines learners' real errors to find their causes, including those not due to L1 transfer.
questions.explanationHi: Error analysis (कॉर्डर) सीखने वालों की वास्तविक त्रुटियों और उनके कारणों का अध्ययन करता है, जिनमें L1 के प्रभाव से परे कारण भी होते हैं।

questions.question: The Language Acquisition Device (LAD) proposed by Chomsky is
questions.questionHi: चॉम्स्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित Language Acquisition Device (LAD) है
options: an innate mental faculty that lets children build grammar from limited input
optionsHi: एक जन्मजात मानसिक क्षमता जो बच्चों को सीमित इनपुट से व्याकरण बनाने देती है
questions.explanation: Chomsky LAD is an innate capacity for language; behaviourist habit formation was what he rejected.
questions.explanationHi: चॉम्स्की का LAD भाषा के लिए जन्मजात क्षमता है; व्यवहारवादियों की आदत-निर्माण की धारणा को उन्होंने अस्वीकार किया।

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conditions for effective use of the Monitor in Krashen's theory?
questions.questionHi: क्रैशेन के सिद्धांत में Monitor के प्रभावी उपयोग की शर्तों में कौन-सी शर्त शामिल नहीं है?
options: Receiving input slightly beyond the current level (i+1)
optionsHi: वर्तमान स्तर से थोड़ा आगे का इनपुट (i+1) मिलना
questions.explanation: The Monitor needs time, focus on form and knowledge of the rule. "i+1" belongs to the Input Hypothesis, not to Monitor conditions.
questions.explanationHi: Monitor के लिए समय, form पर ध्यान और नियम का ज्ञान ज़रूरी है। "i+1" Input Hypothesis का हिस्सा है, Monitor की शर्त नहीं।

questions.question: In the revised Bloom (Anderson and Krathwohl) taxonomy, which language task targets the "Analyse" level?
questions.questionHi: संशोधित ब्लूम (एंडरसन व क्रैथवॉल) वर्गीकरण में कौन-सा भाषा-कार्य "Analyse" स्तर को लक्षित करता है?
options: Listing the characters of a story
Distinguishing facts from opinions in an editorial
Summarising a paragraph in one's own words
optionsHi: कहानी के पात्रों की सूची बनाना
संपादकीय में तथ्य और राय में अंतर करना
अनुच्छेद का सार अपने शब्दों में लिखना
questions.explanation: Analyse = breaking material into parts and finding relationships, e.g. separating fact from opinion. Listing = remember, summarising = understand, original writing = create.
questions.explanationHi: Analyse = सामग्री को भागों में बाँटकर संबंध खोजना, जैसे तथ्य व राय अलग करना। सूची बनाना = remember, सार = understand, मौलिक लेखन = create।

questions.question: In Halliday's functional model, the 'heuristic' function of language is used to
questions.questionHi: हैलिडे के कार्यात्मक मॉडल में भाषा का 'heuristic' कार्य प्रयुक्त होता है
options: explore and learn about the environment, as when asking questions
optionsHi: प्रश्न पूछने जैसे कार्यों से परिवेश को जानने और सीखने के लिए
भौतिक आवश्यकताएँ पूरी करने के लिए
दूसरों के व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करने के लिए
सामाजिक संबंध बनाए रखने के लिए
questions.explanation: Heuristic = learning and discovering (why? how?). Satisfying needs is instrumental, controlling others regulatory, relationships interactional.
questions.explanationHi: Heuristic = सीखना और खोजना (क्यों? कैसे?)। आवश्यकता-पूर्ति instrumental, नियंत्रण regulatory और संबंध interactional कार्य हैं।

questions.question: A teacher gives sentence starters for the first essay, fewer for the second and none for the third. This illustrates
questions.questionHi: एक शिक्षक पहले निबंध में वाक्य-प्रारंभ देता है, दूसरे में कम और तीसरे में बिल्कुल नहीं। यह उदाहरण है
options: gradual fading of scaffolding within the ZPD
optionsHi: ZPD में scaffolding को धीरे-धीरे हटाने का
questions.explanation: Support is reduced as the learner becomes capable of independent performance: Vygotskian scaffolding and its fading.
questions.explanationHi: जैसे-जैसे विद्यार्थी स्वतंत्र प्रदर्शन के योग्य होता है, सहायता घटाई जाती है: वाइगोत्स्की का scaffolding और उसका fading।

questions.question: A learner writes "He goes to school" correctly but says "He go to school" when speaking fast and corrects it when asked. According to Corder, the spoken slip is a
questions.questionHi: एक विद्यार्थी "He goes to school" सही लिखता है पर जल्दी बोलते समय "He go to school" कह देता है और पूछने पर सुधार लेता है। कॉर्डर के अनुसार यह बोलचाल की चूक है
questions.explanation: A mistake is a random performance lapse the learner can self-correct; an error reflects incomplete knowledge and cannot be self-corrected.
questions.explanationHi: Mistake निष्पादन की आकस्मिक चूक है जिसे सीखने वाला स्वयं सुधार लेता है; error अधूरे ज्ञान को दर्शाती है और स्वयं नहीं सुधरती।

questions.question: Prabhu's Bangalore Project is associated with which approach?
questions.questionHi: प्रभु का Bangalore Project किस उपागम से जुड़ा है?
questions.explanation: Prabhu's Communicational Teaching Project used problem-solving tasks rather than a grammatical syllabus: a forerunner of task-based teaching.
questions.explanationHi: प्रभु की परियोजना में व्याकरणिक पाठ्यक्रम की जगह समस्या-समाधान कार्य (tasks) दिए गए: यह task-based शिक्षण का अग्रदूत है।
